author: NBC Palm Springs
title: Cathedral City's Little Food Pantry: Hope vs. Code Enforcement - NewsBreak
text:
9 hours ago
Cathedral City resident Kristina Bruno has transformed her front yard on Brookview Ave into a "little food pantry," a wooden cabinet stocked with nonperishable foods and hygiene products available to anyone, no questions asked. Bruno, motivated by her own past struggles and recent cuts to SNAP benefits, started the pantry as a discreet alternative for neighbors who might feel embarrassed to use traditional food banks, especially during the holiday season.The initiative quickly grew beyond her expectations, requiring her to restock multiple times a day as items are taken and donated. The pantry operates on a spirit of kindness, exemplified by anonymous donors who have dropped off significant amounts of groceries, and by community members who engage in "little trade offs," leaving items they can't use and taking what they need. Bruno plans to expand the pantry to include clothing and blankets for the winter.However, the success of this grassroots effort has attracted the attention of Code Enforcement. While the City of Cathedral City claims to support the pantry, it has issued a field advisory notice, citing concerns over what is appropriate in a residential neighborhood. The notice is described as an educational first step intended to open a dialogue toward voluntary compliance, leaving the pantry’s future availability uncertain.
